tellings.difference: Here Price's intended target was a cabin in the woods and he described a clandestine site nearby instead; Sheehan's telling says Price was given exact coordinates of a CIA facility.

plain: In the 1970s, a man named Pat Price is said to have become so good at remote viewing, the practice of trying to describe a faraway place with the mind alone, that he could describe a secret government site he had never seen. A guest named Dan Sheehan tells it from a file he says he saw, crediting it alongside Russell Targ and Ingo Swann and a document he calls the "Ingo Swann file." In his telling, Price was given "the exact longitude and latitude" of a top-security facility of the CIA, the US foreign intelligence agency, and was able to read a file inside it. A guest named Joe McMoneagle tells it differently, passing on what Targ and Hal Puthoff told him. He says Price was sent to describe "this old Cabin in the Woods" but instead "described a clandestine site" close by. To both tellers, this would mean the mind can reach places that walls and secrecy are meant to keep shut.
